newsitem.title: POLAND: EARLY ZLOTY STABLE VS BASKET, TRACKS DOLLAR/MARK.
newsitem.headline: EARLY ZLOTY STABLE VS BASKET, TRACKS DOLLAR/MARK.

text.p: The Polish zloty was little moved in early Thursday trade with players mainly adjusting to changes in dollar/mark on world markets.
Dealers said the zloty found balance between 0.5 and 0.75 percent above parity and unless large orders materialised the local currency would remain range bound on Thursday.
"The dollar/mark is falling slightly and the zloty is tracking these moves and remains centred around 0.6 percent," said Marek Cherubin, forex dealer at Creditanstalt in Warsaw.
At 0907 GMT the zloty was at 0.66/0.63 percent from parity, against opening's 0.66/0.57 and Wednesday's 0.69/0.66 percent.
The zloty was at at 3.3095/05 to the dollar and at 1.8790/95 to the mark against opening levels of 3.3120/45 and 1.8770/90 respectively.
Dealers said that despite earlier expectations of a slight zloty rebound from Wednesday's close at six-week lows, foreigners continued to sell small amounts of Polish paper today.

They said that if the Polish central bank raised official interest rates by 2-3 points, as a senior adviser on Wednesday deemed would be safe, it would attract hot capital into Poland in the longer term despite the bearish outlook for the zloty.

"If yields were increased 2-3 points foreigners would quickly try to close bad positions in the short-term, but in the longer term there would surely be some inflows," said Piotr Bednarek, senior dealer at ING Bank in Warsaw.
"But I expect the central bank to try to slow domestic demand by increasing market rates and not official rates and such statements are merely testing the waters," Bednarek added.

On Wednesday senior central bank adviser Stanislaw Gomulka told Reuters the central bank saw room for more monetary tightning and that a 2-3 percent rate rise would not spark unwanted hot capital inflows.
Finance Minister Marek Belka said Poland would not issue more bonds on international markets this year but that the country was likely to issue $500 million in 1998.

Belka also said late on Wednesday that year-on-year inflation in June would likely be 14.6-15 percent, against 14.6 percent in May, but that the rate would fall back to or slip below May's level in July.

Overnight rates eased to 22.10/45 against opeing's 22.40/50 and tomorrow/next held flat at 22.29/60 as the money maket had some surplus funds despite a large 1.6 billion zloty central bank drainage announcement. -- Wojciech Moskwa +48 22 653 9700
